originalTitle: Inflation data, Oracle earnings, and an energy supply crunch: What to watch this week
summary: Two questions are set to lead the week: Will the data push the Fed toward a rate hike, and what can Oracle tell Wall Street about the state of Big Tech's AI debt load?
content:
Coming off a bombastic August nonfarm payrolls report that far exceeded expectations, investors step into a holiday-shortened trading week with all eyes on inflation data and earnings from the final hyperscaler of the cycle, Oracle ( ORCL ).

Two questions are set to lead the week: Will the data push the Fed toward a rate hike, and what can Oracle tell Wall Street about the state of Big Tech's AI debt load?

The Nasdaq ( ^IXIC ) was down 0.3%. The S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) was down 0.4%. And the Dow ( ^DJI ) dropped 0.5%.

Coming off a jobs report that saw consensus move a bit closer to pricing in a rate hike from the Federal Reserve in September, investor attention will be focused squarely on Friday's Consumer Price Index, set to give the FOMC a read on the state of inflation that has held above target for five years. Producer Price Index data on Thursday will offer a preview from the wholesaler side of the pricing equation.

How will Oracle's debt load impact AI earnings?

Will inflation data push Fed toward September hike?

What's driving record-high US diesel prices this week?

Which key earnings reports could move markets Thursday?

In the corporate world, Thursday will be the day to watch, with earnings from Larry Ellison's Oracle pulling focus. Given the company's turn toward debt, quarterly results from Oracle tend to act as a bellwether on the state of AI financing. Adobe ( ADBE ) is also set to report on Thursday, coming off a fresh CEO change. Finally, Macy's ( M ) results — also on Thursday — will provide a read on the state of the consumer.

Heading into Friday morning, bets were essentially split 50/50 on whether the Federal Reserve will issue a rate hike in September. The nonfarm payrolls report was expected to show 55,000 jobs added, a fairly middle-of-the-road, low-impact number.

Instead, the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported that the US economy added 162,000 jobs in August, far exceeding even the most bullish of Wall Street expectations — and yet bets on the Fed's September meeting moved only marginally toward a rate hike.

The real test for Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh and the FOMC, economists and market-watchers say, will be this week's inflation data, as Warsh has made price stability the singular focus of his Federal Reserve.

"For the Fed, the jobs report squarely focuses attention on inflation at the next meeting," Bill Adams, chief economist at Fifth Third Commercial Bank, said in a note. "That next decision will be finely balanced. Next week's releases of the August CPI and PPI reports have the power to swing it between a hike and a hold."

That sentiment comes after comments from Warsh himself during his first keynote address at the annual Jackson Hole symposium. During that speech, the chair said the Fed's 2% target for price increases was fixed, and that it's the Fed's duty to rein in inflation running hot.

"Price stability is not self-executing, nor is inflation necessarily mean-reverting," Warsh said. "It is the Fed's job to deliver stable prices."

Inflation has now been running above that 2% target for roughly five years, and as Warsh's comments throughout his public appearances have consistently focused on inflation, the question from investors has become: When are you going to do something about it?

We should get a decent idea of where that debate stands on Friday.

Big Tech will get its final real test of the quarter on Thursday when Larry Ellison's debt-loaded hyperscaler reports earnings, where analysts will be looking for indicators on the company's data center build-out and its financing strength.

The company's shares have fallen by nearly 20% since the start of the year, and nearly 30% over the past 12 months. Much of that has been centered on concerns over the amount of debt Oracle has issued to fund its data center build-out. Yet despite the pullback and fiscal concerns, Bank of America analyst Tal Liani is bullish going into the earnings.

Oracle should report revenue growth for IaaS — "infrastructure as a service," or renting of cloud computing capacity, storage, etc. — of 25% quarter over quarter and 116% year over year as Oracle "expands its data center footprint," Liani wrote. The company's infrastructure ramp should support revenue growth acceleration, and customer prepayments should ease some of the financing concerns that have dominated the narrative around Oracle, Liani said in his note.

"We favor the risk/reward of Oracle, as we believe Street consensus already captures the challenging balance sheet fundamentals," Liani wrote on Friday, "yet is not fully incorporating the likelihood of revenue growth acceleration related to reaching DC buildout milestones."

And don't forget the software offerings, says Liani, even as most focus will be on Oracle's infrastructure business. Bank of America is looking for Cloud SaaS revenue to have grown 12.8% in the quarter, compared to the last quarter's 10.3% growth.

"While Oracle's equity narrative is largely centered on the infrastructure business, we believe the company's traditional software business remains an important component of the investment case," Liani wrote.

US diesel prices raced up to an all-time high on Friday, crossing into new heights as wars in Iran and Russia-Ukraine keep structural pressure on an already tight market for the world's "workhorse fuel."

Prices on Friday climbed to $5.85 per gallon in the retail diesel market, per data from AAA , well surpassing the previous all-time high of $5.816 set in June 2022, months after the Russian invasion of Ukraine that kickstarted a major energy crunch in Europe.

Diesel is a critical fuel for the global economy, underpinning the world's goods trade — from 18-wheelers driving products across the country to the fleet of cargo vessels that sustain the marine shipping market.

chineseTitle: 通胀数据、甲骨文财报和能源供应紧缩：本周值得关注的内容
chineseSummary: 本周将围绕两个问题：该数据是否会推动美联储加息，以及甲骨文可以告诉华尔街有关大型科技公司人工智能债务负担状况的哪些信息？
chineseContent:
在远超预期的八月份非农就业报告公布后，投资者进入了因假期而缩短的交易周，所有目光都集中在通胀数据和本周期最后一家超大规模企业甲骨文 (ORCL) 的盈利上。

本周将围绕两个问题：该数据是否会推动美联储加息，以及甲骨文可以告诉华尔街有关大型科技公司人工智能债务负担状况的哪些信息？

纳斯达克指数 (^IXIC) 下跌 0.3%。标准普尔 500 指数 (^GSPC) 下跌 0.4%。道指 (^DJI) 下跌 0.5%。

就业报告显示，市场共识已接近美联储9月加息的预期，投资者的注意力将直接集中在周五的消费者价格指数上，该指数将让联邦公开市场委员会了解五年来一直高于目标的通胀状况。周四的生产者价格指数数据将提供批发商方面定价等式的预览。

甲骨文的债务负担将如何影响人工智能收益？

通胀数据会推动美联储9月加息吗？

是什么推动本周美国柴油价格创下历史新高？

周四哪些重要的财报可能会影响市场？

在企业界，周四将是值得关注的一天，拉里·埃里森(Larry Ellison)的甲骨文(Oracle)的财报将成为焦点。鉴于该公司转向举债，甲骨文的季度业绩往往成为人工智能融资状况的风向标。 Adobe (ADBE) 也将于周四公布新的首席执行官变动后的报告。最后，同样在周四，梅西百货 (Macy's) (M) 的结果将提供有关消费者状况的解读。

周五上午，对于美联储是否会在 9 月份加息，各方的押注基本上是 50/50。非农就业报告预计将增加 55,000 个就业岗位，这是一个相当中间、影响较小的数字。

相反，美国劳工统计局报告称，8 月份美国经济增加了 162,000 个就业岗位，远远超出了华尔街最乐观的预期，但对美联储 9 月份会议的押注仅略微转向加息。

经济学家和市场观察人士表示，对美联储主席凯文·沃什和联邦公开市场委员会的真正考验将是本周的通胀数据，因为沃什将价格稳定作为美联储的唯一关注点。

第五第三商业银行首席经济学家比尔·亚当斯在一份报告中表示，“对于美联储来说，就业报告在下次会议上将注意力集中在通胀上。” “下一个决定将非常平衡。下周发布的 8 月份 CPI 和 PPI 报告有能力在加息和维持之间摇摆。”

沃什本人在杰克逊霍尔年度研讨会上的首次主题演讲中发表了评论，之后发表了这种观点。在那次讲话中，主席表示，美联储2%的物价上涨目标是固定的，抑制通胀过热是美联储的责任。

沃什表示：“价格稳定不会自动执行，通胀也不一定会均值回归。” “美联储的职责是提供稳定的价格。”

通货膨胀率现在已经超过 2% 的目标大约五年了，而且由于沃什在公开露面中的评论始终集中在通货膨胀上，投资者的问题变成了：你打算什么时候对此采取行动？

我们应该对周五的辩论有一个大致的了解。

周四，大型科技公司将迎来本季度的最后一次真正考验，届时拉里·埃里森(Larry Ellison)负债累累的超大规模企业将公布收益，分析师将在该报告中寻找有关该公司数据中心扩建及其融资实力的指标。

该公司股价自年初以来已下跌近20%，过去12个月下跌近30%。其中很大一部分原因是对甲骨文为其数据中心扩建提供资金的债务数额的担忧。然而，尽管出现回调和财政担忧，美国银行分析师塔尔·利亚尼 (Tal Liani) 对盈利仍持乐观态度。

Liani 写道，甲骨文应该报告 IaaS（“基础设施即服务”，或云计算容量、存储租赁等）的收入增长，环比增长 25%，同比增长 116%，因为甲骨文“扩大了其数据中心的覆盖范围”。利亚尼在报告中表示，该公司的基础设施建设应该会支持收入加速增长，而客户预付款应该会缓解一些主导甲骨文叙述的融资担忧。

利亚尼周五写道：“我们看好甲骨文的风险/回报，因为我们相信华尔街的共识已经抓住了具有挑战性的资产负债表基本面，但尚未完全考虑到与达到 DC 建设里程碑相关的收入增长加速的可能性。”

Liani 表示，不要忘记软件产品，尽管大多数关注点将集中在甲骨文的基础设施业务上。美国银行预计本季度云 SaaS 收入将增长 12.8%，而上一季度的增长率为 10.3%。

“虽然甲骨文的股权叙述主要集中在基础设施业务，但我们相信该公司的传统软件业务仍然是投资案例的重要组成部分，”利亚尼写道。

由于伊朗和俄罗斯-乌克兰战争给本已紧张的世界“主力燃料”市场带来结构性压力，周五美国柴油价格飙升至历史新高。

根据 AAA 的数据，周五零售柴油市场价格攀升至每加仑 5.85 美元，远超 2022 年 6 月创下的历史新高 5.816 美元，而几个月前俄罗斯入侵乌克兰引发了欧洲的重大能源紧缩。

柴油是全球经济的重要燃料，支撑着世界货物贸易——从在全国范围内运输产品的 18 轮卡车到维持海运市场的货船队。

美国在伊朗的冲突切断了波斯湾的成品油供应，而乌克兰军队对俄罗斯各地炼油厂的袭击也导致了石油供应中断。
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于财经市场信号，适合用于观察利率、汇率、股债商品、金融机构和宏观政策变化。
